flip_event_logging.detail: A successful flip logs at INFO (`trust-ir-flip: compiled from trust-ir, did=…`). At the default log level only the WARN `FALLBACK to built MIR` lines are printed, so a build run WITHOUT `RUSTC_LOG=rustc_mir_transform::trust_ir_flip=info` reports ZERO flip events crate-wide and looks identical to a build where the flip is switched off. Any measurement of `fired` MUST come from a log captured with that env var set; the `build.command` below has it.

supersedes.why_the_gate_could_not_notice: `crystal_a1_lineage.rs` RECORDS the lineage digest rather than recomputing it, and it cannot recompute it — re-deriving a body lineage requires running the trust compiler, which the Rust test suite does not do. So the gate only ever checks the fixture's INTERNAL consistency (and for THIS fixture it is weaker still: `crystal_a1_lineage/level_is_zero.rs` reads def_path, lowered, spliced, unsupported, derived_mir.verdict, both FAIL verdicts in a0_criteria, and flip_event.fired — it never reads `lineage` at all). A stale digest here is therefore invisible to every test in the repo; only a fresh compiler run can catch it. That is the whole reason this `supersedes` block exists.
